simple: how full the hall really was, on average, while the kernel ran.
analogy: the rows actually seated, counted every minute; at the end of the evening the hall empties.
precise: the average number of resident warps per SM over the kernel's run, measured by a profiler; it is lower than the theoretical value when the grid is too small, when blocks finish unevenly (the "tail"), or when launches are short.
source: D3 of F6-20 (NVIDIA, "Nsight Compute" documentation (tier 1): occupancy section (theoretical and achieved occupancy).) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a copy from global memory straight into shared memory that the thread starts and does not wait for.
analogy: sending a runner without standing at the door until she is back.
precise: the PTX instruction family cp.async, exposed in CUDA C++ through __pipeline_memcpy_async(dst_shared, src_global, size) with sizes 4, 8 or 16 bytes (header cuda_pipeline_primitives.h of CUDA 12.0); the data does not pass through the thread's registers.
source: H1 of F6-24 (CUDA Toolkit 12.0 headers cuda_pipeline_primitives.h and cuda_pipeline_helpers.h as installed in the build container (/usr/include), read during this build: signature of __pipeline_memcpy_async(dst_shared, src_global, si) — evidence produced or read in this build

simple: a bundle of copies that you will later wait for together.
analogy: all the runners sent out for one tray.
precise: __pipeline_commit() closes the copies issued since the previous commit into one group (PTX cp.async.commit_group); groups complete in order.
source: H1 of F6-24 (CUDA Toolkit 12.0 headers cuda_pipeline_primitives.h and cuda_pipeline_helpers.h as installed in the build container (/usr/include), read during this build: signature of __pipeline_memcpy_async(dst_shared, src_global, si) — evidence produced or read in this build

simple: the bytes you must move even with a perfect cache: every input read once, every output written once.
analogy: every jar carried exactly once, no matter how many dishes use it.
precise: for SGEMM, 4(MK + KN + MN) bytes; it gives the highest intensity any implementation can reach for that traffic level.
source: D4 of F6-21 (Samuel Williams, Andrew Waterman, David Patterson, "Roofline: An Insightful Visual Performance Model for Multicore Architectures" (tier 5; curriculum item 75).) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the version number of a GPU's feature set, and the compiler option that chooses which one to build for.
analogy: the year the hall was built, and which hall the recipe is written for.
precise: sm_XY names the target; __CUDA_ARCH__ is defined in device code to the target's value (800 for sm_80); a binary carries machine code (cubin) for the targets it was built for and PTX that the driver can compile later.
source: D1 of F6-26 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide" (tier 1): warp matrix functions (WMMA), their restrictions and alignment rules; compute capabilities; just-in-time compilation of PTX; __CUDA_ARCH__.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the part of CUTLASS that describes how data and threads are arranged, with one kind of object called a layout.
analogy: the seating charts.
precise: CUTLASS's layout algebra (curriculum: "its CuTe layout algebra"): layouts built from shapes and strides, composed and partitioned to describe tensors and thread-to-data mappings. API names are not given here (unverified box).
source: C1 of F6-27 (Systems Curriculum (this project): 13.2 topic 6, milestones E6 and E7 (quoted), local file SYSTEMS_CURRICULUM.html. A map, not a source (AH-4).)

simple: NVIDIA's open-source C++ template library for writing fast matrix multiplies and related kernels.
analogy: the hall's book of planning rules.
precise: a header library of CUDA C++ templates that organises GEMM as a hierarchy of tiles (threadblock, warp, instruction), named in the curriculum and in NVIDIA's "Efficient GEMM in CUDA" documentation; not installed or compiled in this build.
source: C1 of F6-27 (Systems Curriculum (this project): 13.2 topic 6, milestones E6 and E7 (quoted), local file SYSTEMS_CURRICULUM.html. A map, not a source (AH-4).)

simple: a __syncthreads() that some threads of the block never reach.
analogy: one helper leaves before the "table full?" check, and the others wait for her forever.
precise: a block-wide barrier inside a condition that is not uniform across the block; the CUDA Programming Guide allows __syncthreads() in conditional code only if the condition evaluates identically across the whole block, and otherwise the behaviour is not defined (a hang or wrong results).
source: D1 of F6-22 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide" (tier 1): shared memory (the matrix multiplication example with shared memory), __syncthreads() semantics and its rule for conditional code, compute capabilities table.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: using two buffers so that one can be filled while the other is used.
analogy: two trays: cook from one while the runners fill the other.
precise: a scheme with two shared-memory stages per operand; in iteration t the kernel computes from stage t mod 2 while the copies for tile t + 1 fill stage (t + 1) mod 2.
source: D2 of F6-24 (Wen-mei Hwu, David Kirk, Izzat El Hajj, "Programming Massively Parallel Processors" (tier 3): tiling and latency tolerance.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: two 8-bit formats, one with a bit more precision, the other with more range.
analogy: tiny cups: one with a few more marks, one that holds more.
precise: 1 sign bit, 4 exponent and 3 fraction bits (E4M3) or 5 and 2 (E5M2); in NVIDIA's cuda_fp8.h of CUDA 12.0, E4M3 has no infinities and its conversion from float saturates to the largest finite value.
source: R1 of F6-25 (run of Listing 1 (university/labs/F6-25/formats.log), Cuda compilation tools, release 12.0, V12.0.140 (host code only), exit code 0.) — evidence produced or read in this build

simple: a piece of a small matrix spread over the registers of the 32 threads of a warp.
analogy: the part of each tray that each helper of the row holds.
precise: wmma::fragment<Use, m, n, k, T, Layout>, where Use is matrix_a, matrix_b or accumulator; each thread holds num_elements values whose mapping to matrix positions is not specified by the API.
source: H1 of F6-26 (CUDA Toolkit 12.0 header crt/mma.h as installed in the build container, read during this build: the nvcuda::wmma declarations, fragment specialisations and shapes per type, the __CUDA_ARCH__ guards (≥ 700 for the API, ≥) — evidence produced or read in this build

simple: a layout in which one dimension is itself split, for example "row inside tile" and "which tile".
analogy: "table 2, row 1, seat 3".
precise: a mode whose shape and stride are tuples, such as rows of shape (4, 2) with stride (4, 32): row r maps to (r mod 4) × 4 + (r div 4) × 32.
source: R1 of F6-27 (run of Listing 1 (layout.log), g++ (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 with ASan and UBSan, exit code 0.) — evidence produced or read in this build

simple: the machine instruction that runs a half-precision-input matrix multiply on the tensor cores.
analogy: one pull of the lever.
precise: the SASS mnemonic seen in this build for sm_80 and sm_90: HMMA.16816.F32 (FP16 inputs, FP32 accumulate) and HMMA.16816.F32.BF16; each 16 × 16 × 16 wmma.mma.sync became two of them.
source: R3 of F6-26 (ptxas -v, PTX and SASS counts (resources.log, ptx_wmma.log, sass_hmma.log), sm_80 and sm_90, compiled only.) — evidence produced or read in this build

simple: a note on a kernel that tells the compiler the largest block size you will use, and optionally how many blocks you want to fit on one SM.
analogy: telling the hall manager in advance "rows of at most 256, and I want four tables' worth in the hall", so hands are budgeted to match.
precise: a CUDA C++ function qualifier with a maximum threads-per-block argument and an optional minimum-blocks-per-multiprocessor argument; the compiler limits registers per thread to satisfy it, spilling if necessary.
source: D1 of F6-20 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide" (tier 1): hardware implementation (SIMT architecture, hardware multithreading), the occupancy calculator API, launch bounds, the per-compute-capability technical specifications table.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a rule that turns a coordinate, such as (row, column), into a position in memory.
analogy: the seating chart: "row 2, seat 3 → place 19".
precise: a function from coordinates to integer offsets given by a shape (the extent of each mode) and a stride (the offset step of each mode): index = Σ coordinated × strided. Row-major 4 × 8 is shape (4, 8) with stride (8, 1).
source: R1 of F6-27 (run of Listing 1 (layout.log), g++ (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 with ASan and UBSan, exit code 0.) — evidence produced or read in this build

simple: how far apart, in elements, two consecutive rows (or columns) are in memory.
analogy: how many jars to skip on the shelf to get to the next row of the tray.
precise: the stride passed to load_matrix_sync and store_matrix_sync: for a row-major M × K matrix A, the leading dimension is K.
source: D1 of F6-26 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide" (tier 1): warp matrix functions (WMMA), their restrictions and alignment rules; compute capabilities; just-in-time compilation of PTX; __CUDA_ARCH__.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the first, simplest GPU version: one thread per result, reading everything from global memory.
analogy: Ingrid walking to the pantry twice for every multiplication.
precise: a kernel in which thread (i, j) computes Cij = Σk AikBkj by loading each operand from global memory; it requests 2K loads per output for 2K floating-point operations.
source: D2 of F6-21 (Wen-mei Hwu, David Kirk, Izzat El Hajj, "Programming Massively Parallel Processors: A Hands-on Approach" (tier 3): the matrix multiplication chapters (simple kernel, memory access efficiency). Also NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Best) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a program or function that does the occupancy arithmetic for you.
analogy: the seating chart of the hall.
precise: NVIDIA ships a host-side calculator in the header cuda_occupancy.h (functions such as cudaOccMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor, found in the CUDA 12.0 header in this build) and a runtime API (cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor) that asks the driver for a real device.
source: R1 of F6-20 (run of Listing 1 (university/labs/F6-20/occupancy.log), g++ (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 with ASan and UBSan, exit code 0; the header read is that of CUDA 12.0.) — evidence produced or read in this build

simple: multiplying every value of one short list with every value of another.
analogy: every amount in one hand with every weight in the other.
precise: for column vector a (TM) and row vector b (TN), the TM × TN matrix a·b with elements aibj; GEMM is a sum over k of outer products of a column of A and a row of B (MA201).
source: D2 of F6-23 (Wen-mei Hwu, David Kirk, Izzat El Hajj, "Programming Massively Parallel Processors: A Hands-on Approach" (tier 3): matrix multiplication, thread coarsening.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one round of "load the tiles, wait, compute, wait".
analogy: one filling and clearing of the table.
precise: one iteration of the outer k0 loop; a tiled kernel runs ⌈K ÷ TILE⌉ phases.
source: D2 of F6-22 (Wen-mei Hwu, David Kirk, Izzat El Hajj, "Programming Massively Parallel Processors: A Hands-on Approach" (tier 3; curriculum item 64): the tiled matrix multiplication chapter.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how many binary digits a number format keeps.
analogy: how many marks a cup has.
precise: the number of significand bits including the implicit leading bit; a format with p bits rounds a real number to nearest with relative error at most u = 2−p (in the normal range). FP32 has p = 24, TF32 and FP16 p = 11, BF16 p = 8, FP8 E4M3 p = 4, FP8 E5M2 p = 3.
source: D1 of F6-25 (IEEE, "IEEE Standard for Floating-Point Arithmetic" (IEEE 754) (tier 1): binary16 and binary32 formats, rounding to nearest, subnormals.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how large and how small a number the format can hold.
analogy: how much a cup can hold, and the smallest amount it can show.
precise: set by the exponent field; the largest finite and smallest positive (subnormal) values of each format, as decoded by NVIDIA's conversion functions in this build, are printed by Listing 1.
source: R1 of F6-25 (run of Listing 1 (university/labs/F6-25/formats.log), Cuda compilation tools, release 12.0, V12.0.140 (host code only), exit code 0.) — evidence produced or read in this build

simple: registers are handed out in fixed-size bundles per warp, not one at a time.
analogy: hands are given to rows in packs, so asking for one more hand can cost a whole pack.
precise: the granularity in which the register file is allocated to warps; the toolkit's calculator (cuda_occupancy.h, CUDA 12.0) uses 256 registers per warp for compute capability 8.x, which is why occupancy falls in steps.
source: R1 of F6-20 (run of Listing 1 (university/labs/F6-20/occupancy.log), g++ (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 with ASan and UBSan, exit code 0; the header read is that of CUDA 12.0.) — evidence produced or read in this build

simple: values that do not fit in registers are stored in slow memory and loaded back.
analogy: bowls put on the floor behind the helper.
precise: when the register allocator cannot keep all live values in the available registers, it stores some to local memory (per-thread memory in device DRAM, cached) with STL and reloads them with LDL; ptxas -v reports "spill stores" and "spill loads" in bytes.
source: D1 of F6-23 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide" (tier 1): vector types and alignment, launch bounds, local memory, registers and the register file, device memory accesses.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: each thread computes a small block of outputs and keeps them in its registers.
analogy: Kwame's sixteen dishes made from eight jars in his hands.
precise: each thread owns a TM × TN sub-tile of the block's C tile in an accumulator array that the compiler maps to registers; per k it loads TM values of A and TN values of B and performs TM·TN multiply-adds, an outer product.
source: D2 of F6-23 (Wen-mei Hwu, David Kirk, Izzat El Hajj, "Programming Massively Parallel Processors: A Hands-on Approach" (tier 3): matrix multiplication, thread coarsening.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how many times a value loaded from global memory is used.
analogy: how many helpers cook with one jar before it leaves the table.
precise: the number of multiply-adds performed per operand element loaded from global memory; TILE for this kernel, versus 1 for the naive kernel (ignoring caches).
source: R2 of F6-22 (run of F6-21 Listing 4 (university/labs/F6-21/intensity.log), same compiler, exit code 0.) — evidence produced or read in this build

simple: copy a tile once into the block's fast shared memory, then let every thread of the block use it many times.
analogy: each jar is fetched once, put on the table, and used by a whole row or column of helpers.
precise: a loop over K in steps of TILE in which a block cooperatively loads one tile of A and one of B into __shared__ arrays, synchronises, accumulates TILE multiply-adds per thread from shared memory, and synchronises again before the next load.
source: D1 of F6-22 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide" (tier 1): shared memory (the matrix multiplication example with shared memory), __syncthreads() semantics and its rule for conditional code, compute capabilities table.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: starting the next piece of work before the current one is finished, so that different stages overlap.
analogy: runners already on the road while the cooks cook.
precise: restructuring a loop so that operations of iteration t + 1 (here, its loads) are issued during iteration t; with S stages, up to S − 1 tiles are in flight.
source: D5 of F6-24 (NVIDIA, CUTLASS documentation, "Efficient GEMM in CUDA" (tier 2; named in curriculum E6): software pipelining, multistage mainloops.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one line per version of the kernel, with its speed and the evidence explaining it.
analogy: the kitchen's logbook of every change to the recipe and how long dinner took.
precise: the log that milestone E6 requires: per step, correctness on the shape matrix, registers and occupancy, median time and GFLOP/s at three sizes, percentage of cuBLAS, and the profiler evidence for the change.
source: C1 of F6-21 (Systems Curriculum (this project), milestone E6 (goal, build steps and acceptance tests quoted) and mega project MP3 gates, local file SYSTEMS_CURRICULUM.html and the authoring guide's MP3 card. A map, not a source (AH-4)

simple: one of the buffers in the pipeline.
analogy: one tray.
precise: one set of shared-memory tiles (here As[s] and Bs[s], s ∈ {0, 1}); a kernel with S stages needs S times the shared memory of a single-buffered one.
source: R3 of F6-24 (ptxas -v report for sm_80 (resources.log), Cuda compilation tools, release 12.0, V12.0.140, compiled only.) — evidence produced or read in this build

simple: shuffling the positions inside each row of a shared-memory tile so that a column read touches different banks.
analogy: storing each row's jars in a shifted order so that a column of helpers reaches different shelf sections.
precise: a bijective remapping of addresses, here column → column XOR row on a 32 × 32 float tile, which removes the 32-way bank conflict of a column read without the extra words that padding costs, under the bank model of F6-11.
source: R1 of F6-27 (run of Listing 1 (layout.log), g++ (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 with ASan and UBSan, exit code 0.) — evidence produced or read in this build

simple: a unit in the GPU that multiplies small matrices in one operation.
analogy: the tray machine.
precise: NVIDIA's name for the matrix-multiply-accumulate units of its GPUs, which compute D = A·B + C on small fixed-size tiles for specific input and accumulator types; reached from CUDA C++ through the WMMA API, PTX wmma/mma instructions or libraries. AMD calls its equivalent matrix cores (F7).
source: D1 of F6-26 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide" (tier 1): warp matrix functions (WMMA), their restrictions and alignment rules; compute capabilities; just-in-time compilation of PTX; __CUDA_ARCH__.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: an NVIDIA format with FP32's range and FP16's precision, used inside tensor cores.
analogy: a big cup with few marks.
precise: TensorFloat-32, an NVIDIA format with an 8-bit exponent and 10 explicit fraction bits (p = 11) stored in a 32-bit container; the CUDA 12.0 header mma.h converts FP32 to it with the PTX instruction cvt.rna.tf32.f32.
source: H1 of F6-25 (CUDA Toolkit 12.0 header crt/mma.h as installed in the build container, read during this build: wmma::__float_to_tf32 implemented with cvt.rna.tf32.f32; precision::tf32 fragments of shape 16 × 16 × 8 defined for __CUDA_A) — evidence produced or read in this build

simple: the occupancy the resource limits allow, worked out before the kernel runs.
analogy: how many rows the hall could seat, given how many hands and how much table each row needs.
precise: active blocks per SM computed from the kernel's resource use and the device's per-SM limits, times warps per block, divided by the maximum warps per SM; the value the occupancy API and calculator return.
source: D1 of F6-20 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide" (tier 1): hardware implementation (SIMT architecture, hardware multithreading), the occupancy calculator API, launch bounds, the per-compute-capability technical specifications table.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the outputs one thread is responsible for.
analogy: the bowls one helper fills.
precise: the TM rows × TN columns of C computed by one thread; 1-D register tiling has TN = 1, 2-D has both above 1.
source: D5 of F6-23 (NVIDIA, CUTLASS documentation, "Efficient GEMM in CUDA" (tier 2; named in curriculum E6): thread-level tiling, outer products.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a rule that says which thread owns which elements of a tile, and in what order.
analogy: the chart that says which helper holds which part of the tray.
precise: a layout from (thread, value) coordinates to positions in the tile; WMMA fragments (F6-26) have such a layout that the API hides; library code makes it explicit.
source: R1 of F6-27 (run of Listing 1 (layout.log), g++ (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 with ASan and UBSan, exit code 0.) — evidence produced or read in this build

simple: how far a computed result may be from the reference and still count as correct.
analogy: the head cook's "close enough" rule.
precise: a per-element bound |ĉ − c| ≤ τ, which for floating-point kernels should be derived from the formats and the length of the computation, and scaled by Σ|akbk|, not chosen as a constant.
source: D2 of F6-25 (Nicholas J. Higham, "Accuracy and Stability of Numerical Algorithms" (tier 3): unit roundoff, the constant γn, error of inner products and summation, probabilistic error growth.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the largest relative error of one rounding.
analogy: half the distance between two marks, relative to the amount.
precise: u = 2−p for round-to-nearest; for FP32 u = 2−24 ≈ 5.96 × 10−8.
source: D2 of F6-25 (Nicholas J. Higham, "Accuracy and Stability of Numerical Algorithms" (tier 3): unit roundoff, the constant γn, error of inner products and summation, probabilistic error growth.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one instruction that loads several neighbouring numbers at once.
analogy: carrying four jars in one trip.
precise: a load of a 16-byte aligned float4, compiled to LDG.E.128 (global) or LDS.128 (shared) in this build; the address must be a multiple of 16 bytes.
source: D1 of F6-23 (NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide" (tier 1): vector types and alignment, launch bounds, local memory, registers and the register file, device memory accesses.) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: wait until all bundles except the newest N have arrived.
analogy: "I can cook as soon as every runner except the ones for the next tray is back."
precise: __pipeline_wait_prior(N) (PTX cp.async.wait_group N) blocks the calling thread until at most N of its most recent committed groups are still pending; it covers only the calling thread's own copies, so a block-wide barrier must follow before other threads read the data.
source: H1 of F6-24 (CUDA Toolkit 12.0 headers cuda_pipeline_primitives.h and cuda_pipeline_helpers.h as installed in the build container (/usr/include), read during this build: signature of __pipeline_memcpy_async(dst_shared, src_global, si) — evidence produced or read in this build

simple: the part of a block's output tile one warp computes, and the part one matrix instruction computes.
analogy: a row's share of the tray, and one square for the tray machine.
precise: the middle and lowest levels of the GEMM hierarchy: F6-26's kernel has a 32 × 32 warp tile made of 16 × 16 × 16 instruction tiles.
source: R2 of F6-27 (run of Listing 2 (hierarchy.log), same toolchain, exit code 0.) — evidence produced or read in this build

simple: NVIDIA's C++ interface for warp-wide matrix multiplies.
analogy: the lever and the instructions for the tray machine.
precise: warp matrix multiply-accumulate: the nvcuda::wmma namespace of mma.h, with class template fragment and the functions fill_fragment, load_matrix_sync, mma_sync and store_matrix_sync (all present in the CUDA 12.0 header read in this build).
source: H1 of F6-26 (CUDA Toolkit 12.0 header crt/mma.h as installed in the build container, read during this build: the nvcuda::wmma declarations, fragment specialisations and shapes per type, the __CUDA_ARCH__ guards (≥ 700 for the API, ≥) — evidence produced or read in this build

simple: threads whose tile position lies outside the matrix put a zero on the table instead of reading memory.
analogy: an empty bowl placed where a jar would be, so the recipe still works.
precise: loading 0.0f into shared memory for tile elements with row ≥ M, column ≥ N or k ≥ K, so that the inner loop needs no bounds checks and the padded terms add exactly zero.
source: R1 of F6-22 (run of Listing 3 (university/labs/F6-22/check_tiled.log), g++ (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0 with ASan and UBSan, exit code 0.) — evidence produced or read in this build
